item.title: After 1,600 years, researchers recreate the colour-changing glass of a Roman masterpiece
item.description: A team of researchers has made a groundbreaking achievement by replicating the color-shifting glass of the ancient Roman Lycurgus Cup. Created 1,600 years ago, this unique glass displays stunning optical effects thanks to its tiny gold and silver nanoparticles. Their rigorous experimentation with both ancient and modern techniques opens doors for scientific advancements, extending beyond mere artistic creation. A modern sculpture inspired by this historic artifact will soon be unveiled. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Events in Ireland explore origins of Gulliver’s Travels, the Dublin clergyman’s book that became an instant hit in 1726 In March 1726, an Irish clergyman visited London and arranged for a courier to deliver a manuscript to a publisher under cover of night. The dean of St Patrick’s Cathedral in Dublin knew his novel would cause trouble and wanted to publish it anonymously. His name was Jonathan Swift and the story was called Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World. The satirical work was published that October and is better known 300 years on as Gulliver’s Travels. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Brambles are a problem weed in South Africa, but researchers are closer to finding a natural enemy to manage them
item.description: Invasive alien brambles have been spreading across South Africa since the early 1900s, having come from North America and Europe. All brambles fall within the genus Rubus. item.title: Biodiversity hotspots in southwestern Germany are losing their species richness
item.description: Climate change and shifts in land use are affecting habitats and, consequently, plant diversity. To better understand the consequences of these developments, long-term and comprehensive data are essential. The "Floristic Mapping of Baden-Württemberg," coordinated by the Stuttgart State Museum of Natural History, provides a foundation for this. The data collected over five decades as part of this citizen science project document significant changes in the flora of southwestern Germany, drawing on more than 2.5 million plant observations. item.title: Double debris disk orbiting a dead star hints at our solar system's future
item.description: Astronomers using the European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope (ESO's VLT) have found a rare disk of debris around a dead star that provides a glimpse of what may happen to our solar system. Unlike in similar systems previously found, the debris—the leftovers of planets that once orbited the star—is organized in a double disk, the two parts separated by a clear gap. The disk appears to be shaped by two planetary bodies, one possibly as big as Pluto, that have survived the violent death of the star. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Carlos Martínez Assad: "Los partidos árabes nunca habían votado tanto en Israel"
item.description: La jornada electoral en Israel muestra un escenario que ya estaban contemplados, es decir, que la elección no se decidirá el día de hoy sino luego del juego de alianza de los partidos. Por otro lado, los partidos árabes han mostrado una participación mayor, pues incluso en ocasiones anteriores dichos partidos habían optado por la abstención. Carlos Martínez Assad, doctor en sociología, aborda el tema en France 24. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Israel: First exit polls show no clear winner, Arab parties make gains
item.description: Exit polls on Tuesday showed that the opposition bloc led by Israeli opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot gained a narrow edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud bloc in the Knesset. Likud, however, was projected to be the largest single party in the Israeli parliament. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: ¿Por qué el resultado final de las elecciones legislativas en Israel tarda en definirse?
item.description: Las elecciones legislativas en Israel registraron una participación histórica, en una jornada marcada por ser la primera celebrada desde los ataques del 7 de octubre de 2023. Los sondeos a boca de urna anticipan una contienda muy ajustada entre Benjamin Netanyahu y Gadi Eizenkot, pero el resultado definitivo podría tardar incluso semanas en conocerse. En el sistema electoral israelí, el papel de las coaliciones es clave para formar gobierno e incluso después del recuento de votos, el país podría enfrentar una nueva convocatoria a las urnas. Damian Szvalb, politólogo y analista internacional… Fuente: France 24 - Español.
